page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6455B processor with an x86_64 architecture, featuring 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory consists of 128.0 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 RAM, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The server includes no local instance storage and no integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage architectures over a 6 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded execution driven by the 3.9 GHz sustained clock frequency. The server records top-tier single-core Geekbench marks (2246.0) and top-tier text processing scores (2863.0), complemented by strong throughput in single-threaded compression tests, including 34.6 GB/sec in gzip and 14.94 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. The processor incorporates Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets, assisting lightweight inference operations such as 351.82 tokens/sec for small-model text generation. Multi-threaded evaluations, such as PassMark CPU (28534.32) and Geekbench multi-core (13436.0), place in the middle 50% bracket. DDR5 memory throughput reaches 134.81 GB/sec for large-block reads and supports 22.67 million Redis SET operations per second.

The r7iz.4xlarge optimizes resource density by pairing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with elevated processor clock rates. A primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage, meaning all disk I/O must traverse the 6 Gbps network fabric. This configuration aligns well with workloads requiring rapid single-thread throughput alongside expansive system memory, including in-memory caches, relational database systems, real-time analytics engines, and electronic design automation tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r7iz.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 6455B processor running at 3.9 GHz on the AWS Nitro System. Built on x86_64 architecture, it delivers 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero local disk storage, and no GPU hardware. High base clock frequencies translate to top-tier single-core performance, evidenced by elevated Geekbench single-core results, strong single-threaded compression throughput, and hardware acceleration via AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. DDR5 memory bandwidth reaches 134.81 GB/sec on uncached reads, supporting 22.67 million Redis SET operations per second. With its combination of fast execution cores and large RAM capacity, the r7iz.4xlarge is well matched to in-memory databases, transactional enterprise workloads, and memory-intensive analytics processing.
